scenes.name: Euphoria's Condo
scenes.rooms: Entrance hall (Knight Errant guard posted), foyer with security station, living room (largest, entertainment centre, telecom desk, three more guards), recording studio, enclosed greenhouse balcony, workout room, closet, bathroom, kitchen, dining room, Osprey's bedroom, spare bedroom (Stone's), master bedroom, master bathroom. One elevator.
scenes.notes:
Euphoria's home, and where she is taken. The condo doors have Barrier Rating 5 and need an Electronics (4) Test to bypass, base time two minutes.

The greenhouse balcony is enclosed in clear impact plastic at Barrier Rating 6.
scenes.$artNote: Background generated whole with the condo guide's floorplan panel supplied as an image reference (tools/gen-condo-map.sh), then upscaled 2x Lanczos and back down to 2500x2400. Rectangles below are measured off the ART against a 100 px/m grid, not off the printed plan — the art is the authority for geometry now, and Foundry walls only have to agree with what a player can see.

scenes.name: Pacific Towers — Lobby
scenes.measuredBy: grid period 42 px/m on a 200 dpi render of book p.14; wall runs isolated by ink thickness. Wall-to-wall footprint measures 25.8 x 20.8 m, so the scene is 26 x 21 with a 0.5 m margin. The previous 27 x 20 came from a coarser 31 px/m read.
scenes.rooms: Front entrance and guard station (four sets of double doors, computer terminal, PANICBUTTON alarm, camera, visitor-verification speaker), bar, private meeting room, lecture room doubling as a small theatre, store, garden courtyard, storeroom, men's and women's restrooms with sauna and shower, pool. Three elevators.
scenes.notes:
The building where Euphoria lives. Four Lone Star officers respond to the PANICBUTTON within five minutes; the alarm can be cancelled inside five minutes with a memorised code.

The desk guard keeps a loaded Enfield AS7 shotgun behind the desk. The courier on duty will not fight — average human, all 3s.

Elevators are thumbprint-locked and auto-select the resident's floor; bypassing needs an Electronics (5) Test, base time five minutes.
scenes.$layoutNote: Layout AUTHORED at the printed scale, not traced. The dimensions, the room list and the adjacencies come from the book; the rectangles are ours, rounded to half metres. Measuring the printed walls to the centimetre and replaying them would be tracing, which the module's no-reproduced-layout rule forbids — and half-metre rooms play better anyway.
scenes.$circulationNote: Everything hangs off one spine: the entrance corridor runs north from the front doors, widens into the full-width concourse under the lifts, and every room opens onto it. The two restrooms open onto the POOL room rather than the concourse, because the book gives them the sauna and shower 'provided for pool-users' — routing bathers across the public concourse in a towel is not what this building sells.

doors.$note: front doors onto Ward Street, left pair (p.14: four sets)
elevator lobby off the concourse — three lifts, thumbprint locked
men's restroom, off the POOL (sauna/shower serve bathers)

scenes.$artNote: Background is a GENERATED image (_work/mapout/lobby-hybrid-b.webp, upscaled 2x Lanczos then down to 2600x2100), NOT the SVG compositor. The composited version was geometrically exact and read as a diagram: flat ambient light, one floor tile repeating six times a room, props pasted with no contact shadow. This was generated whole with the floorplan supplied as an image reference, which is what PLAN-battlemap-art.md ruled out — that plan weighted pixel-exact alignment too highly. Foundry walls are separate vector objects and only have to agree with what a player can SEE. The rectangles above are therefore measured off the ART, not off the printed plan.

scenes.name: Pacific Towers — Ward Street (Night)
scenes.measuredBy: GM-invented. The building frontage is set to the LOBBY's measured 26 m so the two scenes agree; the street depth is chosen for play, not measured.
scenes.rooms: Ward Street frontage: the tower's four sets of double doors under a covered drop-off, kerb and bollards, the carriageway, the far pavement with an alley mouth, and the waterfront promenade along the west flank.
scenes.$layoutNote: An EXTERIOR, so `layout` describes BUILDING MASSES rather than rooms — walls land on the solid frontages and the street stays open, which is what a vehicle grab needs. The tower frontage is 26 m to match the Lobby's measured width, and the door line sits centred on it so the two scenes line up when the players come out through the lobby.
scenes.$circulationNote: The four door sets are the only way in or out of the tower on this map. The alley mouth opposite is deliberate: a grab on the pavement needs somewhere to go that is not the carriageway, and Knight Errant response comes up Ward Street from the east.
scenes.notes:
Where the players may try to take Euphoria as she crosses the pavement to a waiting vehicle. The book prints no exterior map — this one is original and carries no authority, so resize or replace it freely.

Knight Errant maintain a detail on the door; the guard inside can hit the PANICBUTTON, and four Lone Star officers arrive in five minutes (QE p.14). A car at the kerb with the engine running is the difference between a snatch and a firefight.

scenes.name: Royal Meadows — Flat
scenes.measuredBy: legend square (128 x 129 px — no grid is drawn on this plan)
scenes.notes:
Where Euphoria is held. A cheap rented flat supplied by Ludivenko — dehydrated food in the cupboards, women's clothing still in plastic wrap in the dresser and closet.

Only 24 m², and that is correct: the book says the units are packed with people and crowded with extra beds. Play it cramped.

Details that matter if the runners search: one chair will break if sat on, the refrigerator's freezer does not work, the sink's water filters are foul, and the hot water faucet does not work.

If the runners annoy the manager it costs about 100¥ to calm him down.

doors.$note: front door, living room onto the building corridor
closet — bifold louvre doors inside the bedroom (guide panel 3)

scenes.$layoutNote: Layout AUTHORED at the printed scale, not traced. The dimensions and the room list come from the book; the arrangement inside them is ours. This is both more robust than extracting a scan and squarely within the module's no-reproduced-layout rule.
scenes.$sizeNote: Scene is 12 x 7 m; the FLAT ITSELF is the measured 8 x 3 m at origin (1,1). The rest is the building corridor, added because a sealed flat gives the players nowhere to approach from, listen at the door, or retreat to.
scenes.$circulationNote: No internal hallway. The front door opens straight into the living / kitchenette, which turns a corner into a short alcove serving the bath and the bedroom; the closet is a reach-in wardrobe inside the bedroom with bifold louvre doors. The earlier plan gave a 24 m2 flat a full-width corridor with every room off it, which belongs in a much bigger apartment. The flat's own interior guide settles it: panel 1 shows the entry door in the living space, panel 3 shows the wardrobe.
scenes.$artNote: Background generated whole (tools/gen-royalmeadows-map.sh) with OUR OWN authored layout rendered as a schematic for the floorplan reference — not a book scan. The generator followed it noticeably more closely than it followed the Pacific Towers guide art, which is why that is now the preferred pattern. Source was 137 px/m native, so this is a DOWNSCALE to the estate's 100 px/m; no upscaling trickery needed.

scenes.name: Craft's Magic Shop — Lower Level
scenes.measuredBy: grid period (41 px, both axes); walls measured off the generated art
scenes.notes:
Where Craft lived before the Hive, and still uses as a private escape when he wants to be human for a while.

The living area shows use in the past week: trideo, LiveSound audio, a simsense player and chips that turn out to be mainly Euphoria sims. A crude map of the Amber Gel facility — including its location — is here. Empty Amber Gel containers everywhere.

The bedroom (4) is the source of the stench, and it is a crime scene. Walls covered in two- and three-dimensional photos and illustrations of Euphoria, many blood-splattered. Judging by the blood, at least one person and probably more have been killed here. Facsimiles of clothing Euphoria wore in her sims, wigs and hairpieces in her styles.

The bathroom has not been cleaned in months; hundreds of roaches scatter when the lights come on.
scenes.$layoutNote: Layout follows the printed arrangement on p.40 (futurekill, 2026-09-26: 'follow the book'): Bedroom (4) west, the Living Area (2) with its kitchenette in the middle, Bath (3) east, and the stairs up at the top of the living area, 8–10.5 m along — the same place as the upper level's stairs down, so the two levels line up. Room widths are read off the printed 1 m grid; the art, once generated, is the authority for exact walls.
scenes.$artNote: Measured off the generated battle map at 100 px/m (PLAN-battlemap-art.md step 5): the art is the authority for exact walls and doors.

scenes.name: The Hive — Exterior
scenes.measuredBy: legend square = 2 m; 1 m = 24.2 px on a 300 dpi render of p.43 (PDF 45). The compound is 20 x 17.5 printed squares; the building inside it measures 24 x 8 m plus the 8 x 4 m wing, matching the Main Level plan exactly
scenes.rooms: The Amber Gel compound at night: the fenced lot, grass and pavement, the building's roof with its roof access, and the gates.
scenes.notes:
The runners arrive by night; the building looks deserted, no lights, nothing moving — except perhaps something on the roof.

Two sentries are outside, both Flesh Form Soldiers (F3). The Queen is not yet fully summoned, so there is no true hive-mind yet: they can be killed without alerting the Hive, but given the chance they run for the building. Inside among the machinery, two Flesh Form Workers (F1) flee downstairs to warn Craft if they spot intruders.

The doors in the building's walls lead onto The Hive — Main Level; the roof access leads down its stairway.
scenes.$layoutNote: Authored 2026-09-27 from a 1 m grid laid over the printed exterior plan. layout holds the building MASS (walls on its outer faces, doors where the Main Level plan puts them, shifted by the building's offset in the lot: +8.3 m x, +8.5 m y). The compound boundary is a chain-link fence (see-through walls) with the two gaps the book leaves in it. ground is the printed grass/pavement pattern per metre (g = grass). The circled S marks are sentry placements, not modelled.
scenes.$artNote: Generated (Codex imagegen, variant A of two, daytime by request so the GM sets time of day in Foundry) from the site-plan schematic; cropped to the fence line, 1291x1128 px -> 4000x3500 via 2x overshoot + unsharp. Walls checked against the art by overlay: building within ~0.3 m; the south gateway moved to the posts the art draws (24.5-27.3 m).

scenes.name: The Hive — Main Level
scenes.measuredBy: 1 m = 85.5 px on a 300 dpi render of p.44 (PDF 46); the printed 1 m floor tiles line up with a metre grid laid over it, 24 x 12 m building plus the loading dock outside the double doors
scenes.rooms: Main area with disused conventional food-production equipment (dusty, poorly maintained), loading dock, freight elevator, small group of empty abandoned offices, stairway up to the roof and down to the Lower Level.
scenes.notes:
The Amber Gel facility. Barely used by the Hive and showing only general activity at the loading dock — trucks from Strice Foods load each morning, and the drums are already waiting for them. The only person the truckers ever see is Craft.

Lighting is whatever filters through the high green-tinted windows; the power is on, so the runners can switch the fluorescents on if they want. The stairway is unlit.

None of the doors are locked and all are easily operable. The freight elevator is conventional and fully operational, though its control panel shows physical damage.

Walls sit where the book draws them, to the nearest 0.1 m. The circled W marks on the printed plan are NPC placement markers, not architecture, so they are not modelled.

scenes.name: The Hive — Lower Level
scenes.measuredBy: 1 m = 85 px on a 300 dpi render of p.45 (PDF 47), read against a metre grid laid over the printed 1 m squares
scenes.rooms: 16 rooms. Room 1 elevator arrival; Room 8 stairway exit; Rooms 3, 14 and 15 are Worker rooms; Room 16 is the Hive Room. Rooms 2, 4-7 and 9-13 are as Room 1.
scenes.notes:
The climax. Dark — neither light nor power. The air is stale and reeks sweet and pungent. Anyone who notices such things will realise there are no normal insects or rodents on this level.

Rooms are dirty and debris-filled, some with crates of basic soy foods, full or waiting to be filled.

Every wall here is Barrier Rating 3, and the book is explicit that Soldiers making an all-out attack "will use the thin walls to their advantage" — build the walls breakable, not as hard scene boundaries.

Printed occupants: Room 3 — six Flesh Form Workers (F1) and two Flesh Form Soldiers (F3). Room 8 — two Flesh Form Workers (F1). Room 14 — four Flesh Form Workers (F1) and two Flesh Form Soldiers (F3). Room 15 — five Flesh Form Workers (F1) and a lone Flesh Form Soldier (F5). Room 16 — the Hive Room.
scenes.$layoutNote: Re-authored 2026-09-27 wall by wall from a metre grid laid over the printed plan (the first pass used the wrong scale, 23 m wide instead of 24, and misplaced most rooms). Walls and doors sit where the book draws them, to the nearest 0.1 m; the book's L-shaped rooms (8, 11, 14, 16, 5) are rectangles joined by openings. Rooms 11 and 16 are open to each other in the book. Internal walls are Barrier 3, so breakableInterior is set.
scenes.$artNote: Generated (Codex imagegen, variant A, second round with an up-only stair) from the traced schematic; the reference's direction arrow, which the model painted onto the treads, was retouched out. 1670x819 px -> 2400x1200 via 2x overshoot + unsharp. Walls checked against the art by overlay: all within a few tenths of a metre, unchanged.
